keyVerseText: And of Kohath was the family of the Amramites, and the family of the Izeharites, and the family of the Hebronites, and the family of the Uzzielites: these are the families of the Kohathites.
rootMeaning: The root of עׇזִּיאֵלִי (ʻOzzîyʼêlîy) comes from the name עֻזִּיאֵל (ʻUzzîyʼêl), which means "my strength is God." This patronymic formation indicates a collective or adjectival form referring to the descendants or people associated with Uzziel. The literal sense emphasizes a familial or tribal identity grounded in divine strength, highlighting a heritage that acknowledges God as the source of their strength rather than merely a tribal label.
usageInScripture: The term עׇזִּיאֵלִי appears twice in Scripture, consistently translated as "of the Uzzielites" or "and the Uzzielites." This consistency in translation underscores its role as a collective noun identifying a specific family group descended from Uzziel. Its usage primarily serves to distinguish this clan within the larger Levitical and tribal contexts, emphasizing lineage and heritage rather than individual characteristics.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding עׇזִּיאֵלִי as denoting the descendants of Uzziel, whose name means "my strength is God," invites believers to reflect on the foundational truth that true strength and identity come from God Himself. This tribal designation is not just an ethnic marker but a reminder of God’s sustaining power over His people. In the Christian faith, this points forward to the ultimate source of strength in Christ, who embodies and fulfills the divine strength that the name Uzziel proclaims. Recognizing such names deepens our appreciation of God’s providence in the lives of His covenant people and encourages trust in His sustaining power.
keyVerseReflection: Numbers 3:27 lists the family of the Uzzielites among other Kohathite families, highlighting their place within the Levitical structure. The use of עׇזִּיאֵלִי here identifies them as a distinct group with a shared heritage rooted in divine strength. This verse reminds us that God organizes His people with purpose and order, and each family, including the Uzzielites, has a role within His redemptive plan. Their identity as "children of my strength is God" enriches the understanding of their calling and service.
